incidents.victim: South Korean Banks and Financial Institutions
incidents.attacker: China — suspected financially motivated threat actor
incidents.vector: AI-powered ARTEX attack tooling combined with Claude AI agents automated intrusions against South Korean financial targets, with confirmed data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Multiple South Korean banks and financial companies breached; data confirmed exfiltrated; South Korean authorities investigating; represents a confirmed AI-assisted financial sector intrusion campaign.

incidents.victim: UK Airbase Used by US Forces
incidents.vector: IRGC-directed operation against a UK military airbase co-used by US forces; specific attack method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: UK government formally attributed the incident to Iran's IRGC; further operational details restricted pending investigation.

incidents.victim: Yandex (Russia's largest internet company)
incidents.vector: Ukrainian drone strikes on three Yandex data centers (Ryazan, Kaluga, Vladimir regions) over five days, targeting physical infrastructure housing cloud and AI compute assets.
incidents.impact: Three of six Yandex data centers shut down or severely damaged; 80+ cloud services disrupted; approximately 64,000 business customers affected; AI supercomputers (used to train Yandex models) potentially damaged; cascading disruptions to payments, email, ride-hailing, and Russian TikTok segment. Cloudflare reported a 50% drop in automated Russian bot traffic.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto GlobalProtect and Prisma Access Users (enterprise)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect and Prisma Access VPN, enabling unauthorized VPN sessions.
incidents.impact: Ransomware actors confirmed using this vulnerability as an initial access vector; organizations with unpatched VPN gateways face immediate ransomware risk.

incidents.victim: ccTLD Registries (.as American Samoa, .gh Ghana, .sl Sierra Leone)
incidents.vector: DNS record modification at the registrar level for three national ccTLD namespaces, with fraudulently obtained HTTPS certificates for targeted domains; Google confirmed its services were among those targeted.
incidents.impact: DNS resolution subverted across three ccTLD namespaces; valid TLS certificates issued to attacker-controlled domains enabling potential traffic interception; full scope of affected organizations under investigation.

incidents.victim: French Supermarket Chain (hundreds of stores)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeting refrigeration control systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, disrupting industrial control infrastructure managing cold chain operations.
incidents.impact: Refrigeration systems disrupted across hundreds of stores, creating food safety risk and significant operational disruption; attack scope and attribution under investigation.

incidents.victim: US Critical Infrastructure (Government, Healthcare, IT, Critical Manufacturing)
incidents.attacker: China — state-sponsored espionage contractor (Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: China's Integrity Technology Group provided command-and-control infrastructure enabling state-sponsored actors to maintain persistent access to US and allied networks via compromised routers and edge devices.
incidents.impact: Multiple US government, healthcare, IT, and manufacturing organizations compromised; Southeast Asian and African entities also targeted; joint advisory issued October 8 by CISA, FBI, NSA, NCSC-UK, ACSC, and partner agencies. Group assessed as contractor to China's Ministry of State Security.

incidents.victim: Enterprise SonicWall SMA 1000 Appliance Operators
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-102255, a maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) server-side request forgery vulnerability in SonicWall SMA 1000 remote access appliances; exploitation confirmed by honeypot sensor data.
incidents.impact: Organizations with unpatched SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances at risk of complete credential theft and internal network access; active in-the-wild exploitation confirmed as of October 2026.

incidents.victim: Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing aviation data subsidiary, valued at $10.55B)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Jeppesen ForeFlight systems via the same Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) exploitation used in broader ShinyHunters campaign; extortion demand issued with threat of exposing sensitive aviation data.
incidents.impact: Sensitive aviation navigation and operational data allegedly stolen from Boeing's Jeppesen ForeFlight division; extortion attempt against a provider of critical aviation charts, navigation, and flight planning data used worldwide.

incidents.victim: US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 across dozens of organizations; FBI systems among those compromised; Accenture failed to patch the platform despite known vulnerability.
incidents.impact: Nearly all FBI special agents' personal and business data stolen, including medical and psychiatric records; 5,000+ FBI personnel records confirmed exfiltrated; Accenture terminated as FBI contractor. Group leader Saif Al-din Khader arrested in Jordan; Dutch member Van der Stap and alleged ransomware negotiation firm co-founder Edward Dubrovsky also arrested.

incidents.victim: ASOS (UK online fashion retailer)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to ASOS systems; attackers leveraged the company's own mobile app push notification infrastructure to announce the breach directly to all customers.
incidents.impact: All ASOS customers notified of breach via mobile app; customer data scope under investigation.

incidents.victim: AI Researchers at US Think Tanks and Universities
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails impersonating a former US government AI official (and Penn center head Alex Engler) proposing research collaborations, then steering targets to credential-harvesting websites.
incidents.impact: Fewer than 10 individuals targeted at think tanks, universities, and research organizations; email credentials sought to access AI research and policy work; attributed to Chinese state-sponsored actors by Proofpoint.

incidents.victim: US Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC)
incidents.vector: Unknown; breach impacted systems holding US Defense Department personnel and eligibility data.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3 million individuals impacted; full data scope and attacker identity not yet publicly confirmed.

incidents.victim: Oracle Health (legacy Cerner healthcare IT platform)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Oracle Health's legacy Cerner systems; Oracle disclosed the breach approximately one year after it occurred.
incidents.impact: 20 million patients affected; delayed disclosure by Oracle raises significant regulatory exposure under HIPAA notification requirements; largest healthcare breach disclosed in 2026.

incidents.victim: Critical Sector Organizations in Spain and Portugal
incidents.vector: Warlock ransomware campaign targeting utilities, telecommunications providers, government agencies, and universities across Spain and Portugal.
incidents.impact: Multiple critical infrastructure sectors across the Iberian Peninsula disrupted; specific ransom demands and recovery status not yet publicly confirmed.

incidents.victim: Denmark Central Population Register
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access through an account secured only with the password '123456', compromising Denmark's national civil registration database.
incidents.impact: Data on 8.8 million Danish citizens (including deceased) stolen; records include names, addresses, and social security numbers covering the entire country's population.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack targeting operational technology (OT) systems at South Africa's national air traffic control authority.
incidents.impact: Air traffic control operations disrupted; incident described as capable of crippling South Africa's entire air traffic management system had it not been contained.

incidents.victim: Government and Organizations in Taiwan, India, Philippines, and Cambodia
incidents.vector: Deployment of novel Antino backdoor malware via spear-phishing targeting government and strategic organizations across Southeast and South Asia.
incidents.impact: Multiple countries targeted; persistent access established via custom Antino backdoor enabling long-term espionage across Indo-Pacific region.

incidents.victim: US Banks and Financial Institutions
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Venezuelan organized crime (Tren de Aragua)
incidents.vector: Malware deployed on US ATM networks enabling cash jackpotting attacks; 1,500+ coordinated attacks across multiple financial institutions.
incidents.impact: $40.73 million in confirmed losses across 1,500+ ATM jackpotting incidents; OFAC sanctioned 10 Tren de Aragua members in September 2026.

incidents.victim: US Government and Enterprise NetScaler Appliance Operators
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two NetScaler zero-days (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772), with web shells deployed on compromised US targets; 50,277+ exposed instances identified globally.
incidents.impact: Web shells confirmed on US government targets; over 50,000 NetScaler instances at risk globally; persistent access established enabling further lateral movement and data theft.

incidents.victim: Financial Services Organization (undisclosed)
incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering via fake video conference invitations distributing GeniexLoader and GeniexRAT malware; targets lured via fraudulent meeting links.
incidents.impact: Undisclosed financial services organization compromised; GeniexRAT remote access trojan deployed enabling persistent access and credential theft.

incidents.victim: Open Source Software Ecosystem (npm, Rust crates, PyPI)
incidents.vector: Compromise of npm ecosystem maintainer accounts including Axios; publication of malicious packages (ChainDrop worm, PolinRider); compromise of Rust arrayref crate and Mastra AI library.
incidents.impact: Malicious packages distributed to downstream developers and projects; ChainDrop worm designed to self-propagate through npm ecosystem; Axios maintainer credentials stolen enabling trust-chain attacks at a widely-used HTTP library.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian Employees at Organizations in France, US, and Canada
incidents.vector: ClickFix campaign using fake CAPTCHA prompts on compromised Ukrainian websites to deliver malware, targeting Ukrainian nationals employed at organizations in France, the US, and Canada.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian diaspora employees compromised; likely intelligence collection on employer organizations in allied NATO nations; represents GRU use of ClickFix social engineering beyond traditional phishing.

incidents.victim: Iraqi Critical Infrastructure and Israeli Organizations
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing using fake Dubai Airports job recruitment lures delivering ShelbyLoader V2 malware; attributed to Iranian state-aligned group operating against adversaries in the Middle East.
incidents.impact: Iraqi critical infrastructure and Israeli entities compromised via sustained espionage campaign (Blinder Tunnel); ShelbyLoader V2 provided persistent remote access enabling long-term intelligence collection.
